performer.name: Astrid, NetComposer Algorithmic Performer (stand-in script on the box, not the netcomposer CLI)

rules_set_by.note: Principle set by Petrus: the Composition gives only chords, bars and tempo shape; rhythm, figuration, texture and timbre come from what the search finds.

composition_ref.music: Johann Sebastian Bach, Prelude in C major, BWV 846, Das Wohltemperierte Klavier I (1722). Public domain.

analysis.credit: Mark Gotham et al., When in Rome corpus

used_from_composition: chord anchors (one per bar, parsed from the Composition text)
composition_ref.not_used: Bach's written notes. No score, MIDI or kern file is read by this Performer.

rule_set.name: search-driven (BWV 846)
rule_set.rhythm: Per section, the next sound in search order with 6+ onsets (rate 1.5-12/s) becomes the rhythm donor. 4-8 of its onsets, time-scaled to a half bar, are the attack times, played twice per bar.
rule_set.figure_contour: At each donor onset, the donor's spectral brightness picks the register: brighter -> higher chord tone among the found notes.
rule_set.notes: Found single notes (one measured pitch class, within 25 cents of A440, no pitch-shift) that are chord tones. Section voice = the contributor whose notes cover the most chord tones; missing tones filled from others in search order.
rule_set.bed: Found chordal sound whose measured pitch classes are all chord tones, with >= 70% of chroma energy in the chord; time-stretched (max 2x) if shorter than the bar.
rule_set.bass: One contributor (best coverage of written bass/root); where it has no matching note the bass is let go.
rule_set.texture: The donor's own audio is heard only when it is unpitched or fits the bar's chord.
